program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 1500

source_provenance: collision screening against merged history, pending Waves 501-1000, and active Waves 1001-1425

policy.validation_strategy: PMID-level dedupe/source verification during authoring; expensive repository-wide validation only after Wave 1500

waves.focus: Randomized crossover trial in 20 healthy adults found sucrose produced the largest acute glucose/insulin response, while aspartame/acesulfame-K resembled carbonated water and sucrose/stevia produced distinct pancreatic-polypeptide and later glucose responses; small acute physiology study only.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of controlled human trials found allulose and tagatose lowered postprandial glucose and insulin, while longer-term cardiometabolic and body-composition effects were limited or uncertain; heterogeneity was substantial for some outcomes.

Randomized double-blind crossover study found erythritol, sucrose and sucralose produced similar learned liking/wanting responses despite different metabolic hormone effects; reward findings were small-sample and mechanistic.

Randomized crossover trial in 19 healthy adults found the sweet protein sweelin did not increase glucose, insulin or GLP-1 relative to stevia and produced far lower responses than dextrose; this is acute formulation-specific metabolic evidence.

Thirty-day randomized double-blind study in 50 healthy adults found D-allulose produced frequent but generally mild transient GI symptoms and no clinically significant laboratory toxicity; short duration and limited population constrain a general long-term safety conclusion.

Fourteen-day randomized crossover trial found sucrose, saccharin and steviol-glycoside beverages produced broadly similar glucose-regulation outcomes in healthy adults, with some within-condition changes and higher triglycerides after sucrose; no consistent superiority of noncaloric sweeteners was shown.

Randomized crossover study across normal-weight, overweight and type-2-diabetes cohorts found acute stevia did not materially alter glycemia, gut hormones, appetite or subsequent energy intake versus water, nor modify glucose responses when co-ingested with glucose.

Secondary observational analysis within a randomized weight-loss trial found decreases in endogenous plasma erythritol tracked with improved estimated cardiovascular risk and atherogenic lipids; association does not establish effects of consuming erythritol.

Two-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in adults with poor sleep found fermented blueberry-leaf tea improved sleep efficiency and wake-after-sleep-onset but not sleep latency, total sleep time or subjective sleep measures; small short-duration functional-food evidence.

Randomized crossover study in 119 healthy adults found yogurt transiently increased yogurt-associated microbes, while adding oats produced little broad effect on SCFAs or host health markers; the healthy microbiome was largely resilient and individual responses varied.

Ten-week randomized blinded trial in 45 older adults found fermented whey protein improved selected physical-performance and skeletal-muscle-mass outcomes versus dextrin placebo, but the formulation also materially increased vitamin/mineral intake, limiting protein-fermentation attribution.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found randomized dairy interventions improved selected global cognition, memory and processing-speed outcomes in older adults, while observational studies were neutral; product heterogeneity and fermented/fortified subgroups complicate category-wide claims.

Pilot randomized double-blind trial in prepubertal boys found fermented and non-fermented milk protein improved short-sprint performance versus placebo, with no consistent fermented-protein superiority and no clear lean-mass advantage; exploratory microbiome findings were noncausal.

Small randomized trial in adults with metabolic impairment found brewer's-spent-grain biscuits increased fiber intake and shifted selected gut taxa/metabolites, while fermented BSG increased HDL; most other metabolic outcomes were unchanged.

Systematic review of eight human intervention studies found kefir produced modest, heterogeneous microbiome changes, with some increases in Bifidobacterium and transient kefir-associated taxa; direct functional or clinical evidence remained limited.

Randomized double-blind crossover trial found a multi-ingredient Korean red-ginseng complex accelerated early ethanol/acetaldehyde clearance and improved hangover symptom scores; proprietary combination prevents attribution to ginseng alone and does not make alcohol use safe.

Six-month randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in healthy adults found Lactiplantibacillus plantarum K014 was well tolerated with no probiotic-related adverse events; GI/common-cold signals were exploratory efficacy observations.

Randomized double-blind trial in adults with recurrent URTIs found fermented noni polysaccharides did not significantly improve the primary NK-cell-activity endpoints in modified intention-to-treat analysis or reduce URTI incidence; per-protocol immune-marker signals were secondary.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 100 adults with functional constipation found a heat-inactivated fermented-milk postbiotic did not improve bowel-movement frequency, transit time, symptoms or quality of life versus placebo despite exploratory neurotransmitter-biomarker changes.

Four-week randomized double-blind trial of a fermented pasteurized oat postbiotic found selective species-level microbiome changes without alpha/beta-diversity shifts; cortisol, IL-8 and well-being signals were exploratory and no clinical efficacy was established.

Eight-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 105 adults dissatisfied with sleep found Lactococcus cremoris YRC3780 improved Athens Insomnia Scale scores and selected sleep-onset/daytime-sleepiness items; strain-specific replication remains important.

Twelve-week randomized trial in adults with overweight/obesity and elevated triglycerides found full-fat fermented dairy modestly reduced waist circumference versus nondairy control, while insulin sensitivity and most other cardiometabolic markers were unchanged.

Twelve-week randomized double-blind trial in healthy women found edible bird's nest produced dose- and time-dependent metabolomic shifts in amino-acid and lipid pathways; clinical significance and health outcomes were not established.

Randomized clinical trial found heat-treated Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LM1004 increased NK-cell activity and altered microbiome-related endpoints, while mechanistic ecosystem data came from simulation; immune-marker improvement does not establish reduced infection risk.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in adults with H. pylori infection found high-dose Lacticaseibacillus paracasei HP7 reduced urea-breath-test values and modestly improved selected gastric markers/symptoms, but complete eradication was uncommon and it is not a replacement for established therapy.
